newsitem.title: INDIA: India seeks questioning of B.A.T on ITC.
newsitem.headline: India seeks questioning of B.A.T on ITC.

text.p: Indian investigators said on Monday they were seeking to question executives of Britain's B.A.T Industries plc who are on the board of Indian tobacco firm ITC Ltd, which is being investigated for alleged violations of foreign exchange laws.

"We have written to the chairman of ITC for interrogation of B.A.T nominees to the ITC board in connection with the $112 million foreign exchange rule violation case," K.K. Kabirpanthi, deputy director at the Enforcement Directorate, told reporters.
The directorate last week arrested a director, two former chairmen and three former executives, in investigations involving a foreign subsidiary of ITC Ltd.
The authorities also interrogated the chairman of the company, Yogesh Deveshwar on Monday.
India's Foreign Exchange Regulation Act lays down elaborate guidelines for companies to follow when transacting in foreign exchange.

"It is B.A.T's usual practise to assist authorities in their investigations wherever possible. We are working with the financial institutions who own about 38 percent of ITC to enable ITC to overcome these difficulties," said a B.A.T spokesman in London.
